name: Boltslinger
body:
Boltslingers specialize in the use of hand crossbows and their fists, adapting their tactics to the close quarters combat that this kind of unique combination focuses on. Filling a room full of bolts before moving in to finish the job, they are consummate professionals when it comes to unorthodox ranged or melee combat.

Class Features
Weapon And Armor Proficiencies

Boltslingers are proficient in simple weapons, hand crossbows and light armor. This ability replaces the normal weapon and armor proficiencies

Fusillade of Bolts (Ex)

At 1st level, the boltslinger can make a fusillade of bolts as a unique full-attack action. When making a fusillade of bolts, the boltslinger can make one additional attack at their highest base attack bonus. When using this ability, the boltslinger can make these attacks with any combination of their unarmed strikes and hand crossbows. Unlike a normal full attack, a boltslinger cannot make any attacks which would be made at a reduced base attack bonus (a 6th level boltslinger could make two attacks at +6, but not a third at +1), including those granted by feats such as Improved Two-Weapon Fighting.

At 7th level and again at 13th level, a boltslinger can make an additional attack at their highest base attack bonus whenever they make a fusillade of bolts. This stacks with the first attack from this ability and additional attacks from haste and similar effects. A boltslinger cannot benefit from other abilities or effects which would grant additional attacks while using flurry of blows except haste effects or the Two-Weapon Fighting feat.

This ability replaces the 1st level of combat tactics, and the 3rd and 6th level of advanced tactics. Boltslingers get their first combat tactic at 7th level, and count their level as class level – 6 for the purposes of combat tactics.

Paired hands (Ex)

At 1st level, the boltslinger gains two hand crossbows. Her starting weapons are battered, and only she knows how to use it properly. All other creatures treat her hand crossbows as if it had the broken condition. If the weapon already has the broken condition, it does not work at all for anyone else trying to use it. This starting weapon can only be sold for scrap (it’s worth 4d10 gp when sold).

Bolt And Fist (Ex)

At 1st level, the boltslinger gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. A boltslinger’s attacks can be with fists, elbows, knees, and feet. This means that a boltslinger can make unarmed strikes with their hands full. There is no such thing as an off-hand attack for a boltslinger striking unarmed. A boltslinger can apply their full Strength bonus on damage rolls for all their unarmed strikes. A boltslinger’s unarmed strikes deal lethal damage, although they can choose to deal nonlethal damage with no penalty on their attack roll. they can make this choice while grappling as well.

A boltslinger’s unarmed strike is treated as both a manufactured weapon and a natural weapon for the purpose of spells and effects that enhance or improve either manufactured weapons or natural weapons.

Boltslingers follow the chart below for their unarmed damage, as well as the damage dealt by their hand crossbows.

This replaces get the job done.

Level	Small	Medium	Large
1st to 4th	1d4	1d6	1d8
5th to 9th	1d6	1d8	1d10
10th to 14th	1d8	1d10	1d12
15th to 19th	1d10	1d12	2d6
20th	1d12	2d6	2d8
